Posterior probability of a higher event probability on study drug with a meta-analytic predictive prior

Source: R/mapbern_post.R
mapbern_post.Rd

Computes the posterior probability that the event probability per unit time on study drug exceeds that on control, from blinded subject-level data, with the mixture likelihood and the meta-analytic predictive (MAP) prior of Brock et al. (2023).

Usage

mapbern_post(
  y,
  t,
  k = 1,
  prior_c,
  prior_d = c(1/3, 1/3),
  rate0 = NULL,
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Event indicators of the subjects (1 if the subject had at least one event).

t

Times at risk of the subjects (positive), in the unit of time of the probabilities.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to control (k:1); Brock et al. (2023) use k = 3.

prior_c

Prior of the control probability: c(shape1, shape2) of a Beta distribution, or a data frame with columns w, shape1 and shape2 of a mixture of Beta distributions, such as the result of map_beta.

prior_d

Shape parameters of the Beta prior of the study drug probability.

rate0

Optional critical value of the study drug probability; if given, it defines the signal instead of rr0.

rr0

Critical value of the ratio \(\pi_d / \pi_c\).

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible intervals.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles are not computed (they are NA).

control

List of settings of the numerical integration, as in exptime_post.

Value

An object of class bssd_post as described in exptime_post, with model "MAPBERN", the probabilities pi_c and pi_d, and their ratio rr. prob is \(\gamma\).

Details

Let \(\pi_c\) and \(\pi_d\) be the probabilities of at least one event in one unit of time on control and study drug. With a constant hazard, the probability of an event of subject \(i\) with time at risk \(t_i\) is \(1 - (1 - \pi)^{t_i}\), and the likelihood of the blinded data is the mixture $$\prod_i [p_B(y_i \mid 1 - (1 - \pi_c)^{t_i}) / (k + 1) + k p_B(y_i \mid 1 - (1 - \pi_d)^{t_i}) / (k + 1)],$$ where \(p_B\) is the Bernoulli probability. The prior of \(\pi_c\) is a mixture of Beta distributions, typically the MAP prior from historical control data (map_beta); the prior of \(\pi_d\) is a Beta distribution, by default the vague Beta(1/3, 1/3) used by Brock et al. (2023). The quantity of interest is \(\gamma = P(\pi_d > rr_0 \pi_c \mid \mathrm{data})\); Brock et al. (2023) use \(rr_0 = 1\) and mention larger values.

The likelihood is that of the exponential Bernoulli mixture model (expbern_post) with hazards \(-\log(1 - \pi)\); only the priors differ. The posterior is integrated numerically on the coordinates \(\mathrm{logit}(\pi_c)\) and the prior distribution function of \(\pi_d\), as in exptime_post.

A prior derived with the RBesT package can be used: the rows w, a and b of a mixbeta object are the columns w, shape1 and shape2 of prior_c.

References

Brock, K., Chen, C., Ho, S., Fuller, G., Woolfolk, J., McShea, C. and Penard, N. (2023). A Bayesian method for safety signal detection in ongoing blinded randomised controlled trials. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 22(2), 378–395. doi:10.1002/pst.2278

See also

map_beta

Examples

# MAP prior from three historical control arms of 100 subjects each
prior <- map_beta(events = c(9, 11, 10), n = c(100, 100, 100))
set.seed(2)
n <- 200
drug <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.75)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(drug == 1, 0.18, 0.095))
mapbern_post(y, t = rep(1, n), k = 3, prior_c = prior)
#> Model: MAPBERN 
#> Tested quantity: ratio rr = pi_d / pi_c
#> P(rr > 1 | data) = 0.8602
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of rr: mean 1.84, median 1.627, 95% interval (0.6569, 4.263)
#> Posterior of pi_d: mean 0.166, median 0.1648, 95% interval (0.09953, 0.2396)
